## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Catuposathiyajātaka* (Ja 441), translated as "The Four Sabbaths", is a canonical story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text is closely connected to the story of Puṇṇaka, with SuttaCentral recording that the narrative of this birth is described within the Punnaka Birth [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus indicates 28 internal Pali reuse matches across two texts [DharmaNexus]. Substantial verse or prose material is shared with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Sattamo bhāgo*), totaling 16 matches (2,394 characters; longest matching passage at §11.1–14.4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, 12 matches (503 characters) are shared with the *Aggaggasamaṇapañha* of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.9), with a prominent alignment at §9.4–9.6 [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring automated cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* (6 matches, including §8.4–9.1) and the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (別譯雜阿含經, T 100; 2 matches, including §9.1) [DharmaNexus].
